seo_title: CBIC Extends ATA Carnet Import Time Limit
title: CBIC Lets ATA Carnet Goods Stay in India Beyond Four Months, Tied to Carnet Validity
court: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
case_name: Amendment to Notification No. 4/2018-Customs (ATA Carnet temporary import scheme)
card_summary: CBIC amended Notification No. 4/2018-Customs, which exempts goods brought into India temporarily under an ATA Carnet from duty. The amendment lets such goods stay beyond the earlier four-month limit, so long as the extension stays within the carnet's own validity period, instead of requiring a separate customs extension application for each shipment.
card_tip: A foreign exhibitor using an ATA Carnet for a trade fair or professional equipment in India should check the carnet's own validity date. That date, not a fresh customs order, now decides the stay beyond four months.
verification_notes: The notification number (36/2026-Customs), its date (13 November 2026) and the point that it amends Notification No. 4/2018-Customs to tie any stay beyond four months to the carnet's own validity are reported consistently by TeamLease RegTech and A2Z Taxcorp. The notification text itself was not independently opened on cbic.gov.in, so the summary is limited to the extension mechanism both sources describe; no figures or procedural detail beyond that was stated as fact.
